title: Finiteness of associated points of a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] which is quasi-compact, meaning that every open covering has a finite subcover. Let $\operatorname{Ass}(X)$ be its set of associated points [def-sc-associated-points]: a point $x$ belongs to this set when the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the annihilator of some element of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Then $\operatorname{Ass}(X)$ is finite. The empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 05AF, lemma-finite-ass, specialized to the coherent structure sheaf and the quasi-compact open X itself.

proof.text: By [pqf-def-locnoeth], choose an affine open covering $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ with Noetherian coordinate rings $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$. Quasi-compactness supplies a finite subset $J\subset I$ with $X=\bigcup_{i\in J}U_i$. For each $i\in J$, every prime ideal of $A_i$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 05AF, lemma-finite-ass, proof for the structure sheaf; Tag 02OK, lemma-associated-affine-open.

proof.text: For each $i\in J$, let $S_i$ be the set of prime ideals of $A_i$ that are annihilators of elements of $A_i$. The $A_i$-module $A_i$ is generated by $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite] with $R=M=A_i$: the ring is Noetherian by Step 1 and the module is finitely generated, so $S_i$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 00LC, lemma-finite-ass; used in Divisors Tag 05AF.

proof.text: Fix $i\in J$ and $x\in\operatorname{Ass}(X)\cap U_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $x$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak p_x\subset A_i$, the canonical map $\iota_i:\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X$ sends $\mathfrak p_x$ to $x$, and $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong (A_i)_{\mathfrak p_x}$. By [def-sc-associated-points], some $z\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has annihilator the maximal ideal. A ring isomorphism preserves units, hence the unique maximal ideals of these local rings, and sends the equation $az=0$ to the identical annihilator equation for the image of $z$. Thus the maximal ideal of $(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_x}$ is the annihilator of an element of its regular module, which is the localization of the $A_i$-module $A_i$. Since $\mathfrak p_x$ is finitely generated by Step 1, [lem-sc-associated-localization-fg] applied with $R=M=A_i$ shows that $\mathfrak p_x$ is the annihilator of an element of $A_i$. Therefore $\mathfrak p_x\in S_i$, and $x\in\iota_i(S_i)$.

source.place: Tag 05AF, lemma-finite-ass, proof for the structure sheaf; Tag 02OK, lemma-associated-affine-open.

proof.text: Every associated point belongs to some $U_i$ with $i\in J$, so Step 3 gives $\operatorname{Ass}(X)\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in J}\iota_i(S_i)$. Each image $\iota_i(S_i)$ is finite by Step 2; their union is finite because $J$ is finite. A subset of a finite set is finite. When $X$ is empty its associated-point set is empty, so the conclusion includes this case.
